PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.dashboard.byCoach.job: Start each day with one concrete activity — apply for a job, update your CV, or reach out to a contact.
You don't need to do everything at once. Three small steps a day are better than one big step that never happens.
The page is split into four parts: job search, career, resources, and your everyday life. Under each heading you'll see what you've already done there — click a row to continue.
Where do I start if I'm completely new here?

Start with your profile — the more you fill in there, the better job suggestions you get. Then do the Interest Guide (10 minutes), then build your CV with the templates. All of this builds the basis for the matching in Search Jobs.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.dashboard.byCoach.men: One thing at a time. Close everything else and choose one task for today.
It's okay not to do something job-search related every day. Rest counts too.
Log how you feel in the diary — you'll see more clearly what gives you energy once you have some data.
I feel overwhelmed by everything here. What do I do?

That's completely normal. Close everything except Overview. Choose ONE thing today — just one. Maybe call a contact or read an article. Build momentum back up step by step. The diary feature helps you see patterns in what gives you energy and what drains it.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.jobbHub.byCoach.jobbc: Start with your CV if you're new here. Both the cover letter generator and the job matching read it, so what you fill in once gets used in several places.

Speculative Application searches for companies, not job ads. The details come from the Bolagsverket (Swedish Companies Registration Office) register, so the address and registration number are correct.
If you've applied for a job somewhere else, add it under Applications anyway. That's where you can see what's waiting for a reply.
Which tool should I start with?

CV first, cover letter next, then job search. The cover letter pulls details from your CV, and the job search matches against what you've filled in. Do it in reverse order and you'll end up doing the same work twice.
Does the portal apply for jobs for me?

No. The portal finds job ads, writes drafts, and keeps track of what you've applied for — but you submit the application yourself, to the employer. There's no button here that sends anything to a company.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.jobbHub.byCoach.menta: Decide in advance how many jobs you'll apply for this week. A number you can manage beats an ambitious one you don't.
A rejection says nothing about you as a person. Most people apply for many jobs before one works out.
Don't have the energy to apply today? Do an interview exercise instead — it doesn't require an application and you can stop whenever you want.
I've been applying for a long time without any replies. What do I do?

Change one thing, not everything. Try speculative applications for a week — reaching out to companies that haven't advertised often gets more replies, because you're not competing with a hundred other applicants. And bring up the pattern with your consultant; it might come down to something small in your CV.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.karriarHub.byCoach.st: The Interest Guide is based on how you answer, not on your CV. That's why it can suggest jobs you've never thought of — four short parts to answer.
The Skills Gap Analysis compares your CV against a job you choose yourself. Paste in a real job ad, and the gap becomes concrete instead of general.
The figures under Labor Market come directly from Arbetsförmedlingen (the Swedish Public Employment Service) and change daily.
Do I need to know what I want before I start?
No — that's the whole point of the Interest Guide. It asks questions about what you like doing and suggests jobs based on your answers. You can redo it later; the answers aren't set in stone.
Does the portal show what an education costs?

No. The education search shows what's available and where, but not student aid or fees. That's decided by CSN (the Swedish student aid authority) and the school — ask them before you turn anything down.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.karriarHub.byCoach.jo: A goal you can act on tomorrow is worth more than one that describes 2030. Set the short-term one first.
Personal branding isn't an ad. It's being able to say what you're good at in two sentences, without hesitating.
A skill you're currently learning is worth writing down. "In progress: basic Excel" shows direction.
Is it too late to change career path?

First map out what you already have — the skills gap analysis often shows the distance to a new job is smaller than you thought. Many career changes don't need a new degree, just the ability to put words to what you already know.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.resurserHub.byCoach.d: The Knowledge Base is searchable. Type what you're wondering about in your own words instead of browsing through the categories.

External Resources are links out of the portal — Arbetsförmedlingen, Försäkringskassan (the Swedish Social Insurance Agency), and others. They open in a new tab, so you don't lose what you're working on.
Print Resources makes a PDF of what you check off. Good if you'd rather read on paper or want to bring something to a meeting.
The AI Team is five specializations of the same AI. If you get an answer that doesn't fit — switch agent and ask again.
Yes, on your account, so you can read them again. You can also export a conversation as a PDF or clear the chat completely, using the buttons at the top of the AI Team.
Where does what I write to the AI go?

To an AI service outside the portal — that's what formulates the answer. Personal identity numbers and account numbers are removed before the text is sent there. The rest is described in the privacy policy, and it's worth reading before you paste in anything sensitive.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.resurserHub.byCoach.s: Read one article at a time and do what it suggests before you read the next one. Ten articles read without action give you less than one carried out.
Bookmark what you want to come back to — your bookmarks are collected under Your Documents.
Where do I find my own things?
Under Your Documents. That's where your CV, your cover letters, saved jobs, and bookmarked articles are — all in one place.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.vardagHub.byCoach.arb: The calendar here is standalone — it doesn't sync with Google or Outlook. If you also keep your meetings there, you'll need to add them in both places.
The exercises are saved to your account. You can start one, close your computer, and continue another day.
Logging how you feel requires your consent, because it counts as health data. You can withdraw your consent whenever you want.
Do I have to log how I feel every day?
No. The point is to see patterns over time, not to fill in a row. If you log a few times a week, the curve still shows — and if you skip a month, nothing happens.
How do I plan a day when I have little energy?

Put what needs the most mental effort where you've historically had the most energy, and put only ONE such thing per day. Let the rest be simple things. If your mood curve shows afternoons are hard — don't book anything then.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.vardagHub.byCoach.men: Only you see the diary. Your consultant has no way into it — so write what you actually feel, not what you think someone wants to read.
Keep it short. Three sentences are enough: what happened, how I felt, what I'll do tomorrow.
A bad day is information, not a failure. It tells you something about what takes energy.
What does my consultant see of this?
Only what you've shared. Under My Consultant there's a list showing exactly which parts are visible and which only you see, and you change that there. The diary isn't included — it's always yours.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.profile.byCoach.jobbc: Desired occupations are gold — fill in 3-5 jobs you're interested in, and rank them. That's what drives the matching in Search Jobs.
Be specific in the "location" field — "Stockholm" gives more matches than "the Stockholm area".
Work preferences (full-time/part-time, remote) narrow the job feed and show only jobs that fit you.
How many desired occupations should I add?

2-5 is a good amount. Put the job you want most at the top (priority 1). It helps if you choose from the list (with a green check) — then the job matches exactly in Arbetsförmedlingen's system. Free text also works but is less precise.
What does the "How I Work Best" section do?

It's called "How I Work Best" in your profile — what you need for a job to work: shorter shifts, quiet rooms, visual support, and so on. Right now, only you can see it. Neither employers, your consultant, nor Arbetsförmedlingen get it automatically. If you want your consultant to know something from it, tell them directly.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.profile.byCoach.digit: Everything saves automatically — you don't need to press a save button. Green check = saved to the cloud.
If you've built your CV here, you can fill in your profile from it with the "Import CV" button. It pulls from your Jobin CV — a file you upload under Documents isn't read automatically.
The profile status meter shows what's missing — click "Next step" to go straight there.
In the Supabase cloud. You can log in from any device and see the same data. Nothing is saved only locally in the browser. If you log in on your phone, you'll see the same profile there.
What does the avatar upload do?

The picture you upload shows on your profile page and in your CV if you choose a template that has a photo. It isn't shared with employers automatically — only if you include the CV yourself in an application.
Fill in your profile from your CV
Ask more in the AI Team
Write your work experience as TASKS, not RESPONSIBILITIES. "Picked 80 orders a day" is stronger than "responsible for picking".
Add numbers when you can — "reduced errors by 12%", "led 5 training sessions". Concrete equals credible.
One page is often enough. If your CV spills onto page 2, shorten older jobs and focus on the last 5 years.
Do I need to include jobs from before 2010?

Only if they're directly relevant to the job you're applying for now. Otherwise, group them under "Earlier experience: 2003-2010 — various jobs in service and retail". Save the space for what matters.
How do I write about it if I've been away from the job market for a while?
Be open and brief. "2022-2024: parental leave" or "2023-2024: rehabilitation — now ready to start working" is enough. Employers appreciate honesty more than vague wording.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.cv.byCoach.digitalcoa: Choose a template first — different templates suit different industries (Berlin = creative, Centered = classic).
The preview updates live as you type. Use the Eye button for full screen.
Export as PDF for applications; Word if the employer needs to be able to edit it.

For healthcare/education/public sector — "Centered" or "Nordic". For office/admin — "Manhattan" or "Executive". For creative jobs — "Berlin" or "Atelier". You can switch templates at any time without losing data.
My PDF looks strange — what do I do?

Press the Eye button and check it page by page. If text spills over: shorten sections. If the photo looks pixelated: upload a larger photo in your profile. Contact support if the problem doesn't go away.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.jobSearch.byCoach.job: Set the occupation filter before the location filter — it gives broader and more relevant results.
Click "Get from profile" if you've already added desired occupations there, so you don't have to repeat yourself.
Save interesting jobs with the bookmark — that way you'll find them quickly under Saved.
Save your favorite searches as job alerts — next time you open the page, it will show how many new jobs have appeared since last time.
Not many results — what do I do?

Widen the filter: remove the employment type, drop the location (or choose the whole region), or pick broader occupation categories. Use "Last month" instead of "Last week". You can also try a free-text search without an occupation filter.
There are a lot of irrelevant results — can I filter them out?

Use several occupations at once (OR matching) — that narrows the results to just those. Also add a specific location. If the jobs are still irrelevant, try updating the CV skills in your profile so the matching gets smarter.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.jobSearch.byCoach.men: Set a limit — for example "I'll browse for 30 minutes in the morning, then close it". Otherwise it can feel endless.
Sort out jobs you do NOT want just as actively as you save the ones you do. Less to scroll through.
Rejections aren't personal. The statistics show that people apply for many jobs before one works out — that's normal.
I feel down after a rejection — how do I handle it?

That reaction is normal — rejections always feel hard. Note the day in your diary so you can see patterns. To recover: do something physical (a walk), write down one thing you did well in the application, wait at least 24 hours before applying for the next one. Longer term: talk to your consultant about your best qualifications to get some perspective back.
Write about the day in the diary
Ask more in the AI Team
Log every application as soon as you send it — that way you'll have the details for follow-up and statistics.
The status "Interview booked" → "Rejected/Offer" — update as soon as something happens.
Note the contact person, phone number, and deadlines — that way you won't lose track.
How long should I wait before I follow up?

If the job ad states when a decision is expected — wait at least 3 days after that. Otherwise: 7-10 days after you submitted it. Short, friendly follow-up emails are fine; only call if you've already been in contact.
Ask more in the AI Team
Don't count rejections as failures — count jobs APPLIED FOR as progress. You did the work.
If you need a break — take one. The list will wait.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.coverLetter.byCoach.j: Write WHY you want this specific job — not just that you're interested.
Link at least one concrete experience to something in the job ad. "I have 2 years of warehouse experience — that matches your requirements."
Keep it to 1 page (3-4 paragraphs). Longer letters don't get read.
Do I need to write a cover letter for every application?

Not always — many jobs only ask for a CV. When the ad asks for a cover letter, tailor it to that specific job. A generic letter is spotted in 5 seconds and ends up in the trash. Five tailored letters beat fifty generic ones.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.coverLetter.byCoach.d: The AI assistant can generate a first draft — then you edit it so it sounds like you.
Paste the job ad into the "Job ad" field — then the AI adapts to that specific role.
Save different versions for different industries — you don't need to start over every time.
Is it okay to send AI-generated cover letters?

As a DRAFT, yes. But read it through and adjust it — otherwise it feels generic, and all AI letters start to sound the same. At least rewrite the opening and one concrete experience in your own words.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.spontaneous.byCoach.j: Speculative applications get a higher response rate than replies to job ads — the company doesn't even know they need you yet.
Put your energy into MOTIVATION (why this company) and VALUE (what I bring) — not CV details.
Follow up after 7-10 days with a short email or a phone call.

Companies within commuting distance that are neither huge nor the very smallest are usually the easiest to reach: the biggest have rigid processes, and the smallest have no one to handle applications. We don't have an exact ideal size — but that's where you have the best chance of reaching an actual person.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.spontaneous.byCoach.m: One speculative application a week is more than most people do. Set a realistic pace.
Rejection for speculative applications is often just silence — that doesn't always mean no, sometimes it just means "we have nothing right now".
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.interviewSimulator.by: Use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Concrete equals convincing.
Prepare 3 stories about yourself — one about a success, one about a challenge, one about a mistake you learned from.
Have a question ready to ask — it shows engagement. "What does a typical work year look like here?" always works.
What do I do if I get nervous?

Practice, practice, practice. Use the simulator here at least 5 times before the real interview. Breathe deeply using 4-7-8 (in for 4s, hold for 7s, out for 8s) in the car beforehand. It's okay to say "Good question, let me take a second to think". Silence is not your enemy.
Ask more in the AI Team
Nervousness isn't the opposite of confidence — it's energy. You can channel it.
You're interviewing the employer just as much as they're interviewing you. Is this the right place for you?
I completely freeze up in interview situations.

You're not alone. Practice a low-risk simulation first (with the voice turned off), then a full simulation. For real interviews: ask for a phone interview first instead of video — less stimuli, easier to focus. And talk to your consultant about coaching before big interviews.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.interestGuide.byCoach: Answer intuitively — your first instinct is usually right. Don't think "what should I answer".
The result isn't a verdict — just a perspective. You can be strong in several types.
Once you have your result, check the job suggestions — some might be completely new to you and worth exploring.

A psychological model that divides work interests into 6 types: Realistic (hands-on), Investigative (analytical), Artistic (creative), Social (people-focused), Enterprising (leadership/sales), and Conventional (structure/data). It was developed by John Holland and is used internationally for career guidance. The result shows your THREE strongest types — not just one.
Skills Gap Analysis after the guide
Ask more in the AI Team
There's no "wrong" answer. Your answers are saved after each question, so you can leave the page and continue later.
Be kind to yourself — you don't need to fit into a box.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.career.byCoach.studie: Think in stages, not end goals — what's your next reasonable step (6-12 months)?
List 3-5 jobs you're curious about, not just one. It's okay to have several paths.
Career planning isn't a fixed map — it's a compass. The direction matters more than the exact route.
I don't know what I want to become — where do I start?

Completely normal. Do the Interest Guide first — it gives you 3 strong areas. Then look at the jobs linked to your top results. Narrow it down to 2-3 that sound interesting, read about them, talk to someone who works in that field. You don't need to know exactly what you want to become — just which direction you're heading.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.career.byCoach.jobbco: Before you invest in education — try an internship or work training in the field. Many jobs look different in reality than they do in the brochure.
Some jobs don't require the education you think they do. Check job ads in the field — what do the requirements actually say?
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.education.byCoach.stu: Before you start a long program — try shorter courses in the field first. Many YH (higher vocational education) programs admit students without formal qualifications if they've shown interest.
CSN (student aid) and study start support exist for different life situations — check what you're entitled to BEFORE you turn down an education.
Validation of prior learning (RPL) can shorten the length of your studies. Ask the school about it.
Komvux, YH, or folkhögskola — what suits me?

Komvux (municipal adult education): upper secondary grades you're missing (1-2 years, CSN). YH (higher vocational education): vocational training, 1-2 years, often with an internship and strong employability (CSN). Folkhögskola (folk high school): broad general or vocational focus, fewer requirements, often good if you need to rebuild confidence and study skills (CSN for 1-year programs, plus possibly study start support).
I have trouble reading and writing — can I still study?

Yes. Schools offer support: dyslexia support, adapted exams, a mentor, text-to-speech. If you have a disability, you may get financial support through Arbetsförmedlingen and an adapted study pace. Tell the school when you apply — they'll help.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.skillsGapAnalysis.byC: Focus on 2-3 skills you genuinely lack — not 15. Gradual progress beats everything.
Recent skills (from the last 5 years) usually carry more weight than old ones in applications.
Some skills are learned fastest through internships or volunteer work, not courses.
Set one skill as a 3-month goal and one as a 6-month goal. That's realistic.
Add the skills to your CV even while you're learning them — "in progress: basic Excel". It shows development.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.linkedinOptimizer.byC: The profile photo makes the biggest difference of all — LinkedIn itself says a profile with a photo gets noticeably more views. A clear face, a light background, a smile.
The headline field should NOT just be your job title — write "Warehouse worker looking for the next step" or "Seeking an occupational therapist role in Stockholm".
Ask for recommendations from former colleagues and managers — 3-5 go a long way.

You don't need to post at all to find a job through LinkedIn. But 1-2 posts a month commenting on something in your field increases visibility. It's better to comment on other people's posts consistently than to post your own rarely.
Ask more in the AI Team
Turn on the "Open to work" badge — recruiters search using that filter.
List 3-5 job roles you're open to in "Career interests".
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.personalBrand.byCoach: Personal branding isn't about Instagram — it's about being consistent. The same core words on your CV, on LinkedIn, and in interviews.
Choose 3 words that describe you professionally. Use them as a thread running through all your material.
You don't need to be "visible on social media" to have a clear personal brand. A clear CV is enough.
What do people say about you when you're not in the room? That's your real brand.
Ask 3 people you've worked with to describe you in 3 words. The pattern is your brand.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.salary.byCoach.jobbco: Do your research BEFORE the interview — check Saco's or Unionen's salary statistics for your occupation code (SSYK).
Never say the first number if you can avoid it — ask "what have you budgeted for this role?"
If they push you: give a range ("38-44k SEK, depending on responsibility"), not an exact number.
Is it okay to negotiate even if I've been out of work for a long time?

Yes — you're worth just as much no matter how long you've been searching. But negotiate reasonably — check the statistics first. Fixating on an exact number can cost you the offer; also listen to what the job includes (vacation, wellness benefits, working from home) — that counts as "pay" too.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.international.byCoach: EU/EEA — you can work without a visa. Norway, Denmark, and Germany have large employers looking for Swedish workers.
Send your CV in English or the local language. Don't translate mechanically — adapt it to the norms of that country.
EURES (Europass) is the official EU job portal — a good place to start.
Some Swedish qualifications aren't always recognized abroad — check EU-NARIC for a reference assessment.
Erasmus+ for study and internships lasting 2-12 months is open to many vocational programs.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.settings.byCoach.digi: Switching themes (light/dark) is personal — choose whichever is easier on your eyes.
You can turn off notifications by category — you won't miss anything important if you turn off marketing.
The language selector is up in the top menu, not on this page — change it there if you want the app and the AI to respond in a different language.
Where do I turn the coach tips on or off?

In the "Appearance" section on this page there's a "Show coach tips" toggle. You can turn it off if it feels like visual clutter — all the tips are still available in the AI Team if you want to reach them manually.
How do I delete my account?

Under the Privacy tab, at the bottom, there's "Delete account". The deletion happens 14 days later — you can still change your mind during that time, after which everything is gone permanently. If you just want to pause — log out and turn off notifications, and the account will sit dormant.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.diary.byCoach.mentalc: Don't write long entries — 3 sentences are enough. "Today I felt X. It was triggered by Y. Tomorrow I'll do Z."
Patterns are more interesting than individual days — after 2 weeks you'll see what gives you energy versus what drains it.
It's okay not to write every day. Write when it feels important.

Only you. Not your consultant, not Arbetsförmedlingen, not Jobin. The diary never leaves your account, no matter what you write here. If you want to tell your consultant something from it, you'll need to do that yourself — in a meeting or a message. There's no button that shares it.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.diary.byCoach.arbetst: Note your energy level (1-5) along with your daily entry — you'll see the connection between activity and mood.
Weekly summaries (Sunday evening) are great for spotting trends.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.wellness.byCoach.ment: Consistency beats intensity. 10 minutes of meditation a day beats 1 hour once a week.
Sleep is the foundation — without sleep, nothing else works. Prioritize it first.
Note what RESTORES your energy (not just what drains it) — that's your toolbox.
I'm not doing well — are the exercises here enough?

The exercises here are support, not treatment. If you've been feeling down for more than 2 weeks, you've lost your sleep, or you've lost your appetite — seek care. Call 1177 (Swedish healthcare advice line) or book an appointment at your health center. If you're in ACUTE distress or having thoughts of suicide — call 112 (emergency) or 90101 (the suicide helpline).
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.wellness.byCoach.arbe: Energy balance, not time balance. Some activities give you 100% energy, others take 100%. Plan your day for maximum balance.
Structure the DAY, not just the week. Morning routine + midday routine + evening routine.
Break long stretches into shorter ones. 25 minutes of work plus a 5-minute break is often more effective than 1 hour without a break.
How do I know if I'm taking on too much?

Three signs: 1) You're sleeping worse, 2) You're getting irritable more easily, 3) You don't have energy for things you enjoy. If 2 out of 3 apply — remove something. You don't need to fix everything in the same week.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.calendar.byCoach.arbe: Schedule recovery time like meetings — otherwise it becomes "free time" that easily gets eaten up by other things.
Put job-search sessions during your strongest time of day — not the last hour.
Leave a buffer between meetings (15 minutes) — you need time to switch gears.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.calendar.byCoach.jobb: Schedule dedicated "job search time" 2-3 times a week. If it's not in the calendar, it doesn't happen.
The calendar here is standalone — it doesn't sync with Google or Outlook. If you also keep your meetings there, you'll need to add them in both places.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.exercises.byCoach.men: One exercise done beats three planned. Start small.
If you've started an exercise, you can find your way back to it via the "Started" filter at the top.
Some exercises feel strange the first time — give them 2-3 tries before you judge them.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.exercises.byCoach.arb: Breathing exercises work physiologically even if they feel awkward. It's not placebo.
Grounding exercises are great for acute stress — "5 things I see, 4 I hear, 3 I feel".
Your consultant is there for YOU — ask questions even if they feel "silly".
Prepare 2-3 things you want to talk about before the meeting — otherwise time slips away.
Be honest about what isn't working — your consultant can't help with things you hide.

That you're active — applying for jobs, filling in plans, coming to meetings. You don't need to be perfect; just show that you're trying. Say something if things aren't working (illness, feeling down, any kind of crisis) — your consultant can help adjust things.
Ask more in the AI Team
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.knowledgeBase.byCoach: Use the search function — you'll find things faster than by scrolling.
Bookmark articles you keep coming back to. You have your own personal reading list.
Longer articles have a table of contents — jump straight to the relevant section.
The thin line at the top fills in as you read, so you can see how far you've come.
If you want an article on paper, use your browser's print function (Ctrl+P) — we don't have our own export button.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.resources.byCoach.dig: Here's what you've saved in Jobin: your CV, your cover letters, saved jobs, and bookmarked articles. Links to Arbetsförmedlingen, Försäkringskassan, and others are under External Resources.
Bookmark an article using the bookmark icon in the row above the article text, and you'll find it back here.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.resources.byCoach.stu: Arbetsförmedlingen, Försäkringskassan, and Skatteverket (the Swedish Tax Agency) have a lot of free material — we link to the most important ones.
PAGE_COACH_CONTENT.aiTeam.byCoach.digita: Choose the right agent for the task — Career Coach for applications, Mental Coach for stress, and so on.
Be specific in your question — "Help me rephrase point 3 in my CV" beats "Help me with my CV".
You can copy the AI's answer and paste it into other tools.

The AI is great at helping you phrase things, brainstorm, and check logic. But it can be wrong about facts (laws, regulations, dates). Always verify factual information with official sources (Arbetsförmedlingen, Skatteverket, your health center).
